text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The National Assembly currently sitting without opposition parties in Zomba, more than 60km north east of Blantyre, on Thursday unanimously supported a motion to punish all boycotting members of parliament by withdrawing their allowances and salaries.

- Fiscal Police in Lilongwe, central Malawi, on Wednesday arrested seven senior government officials in the Lands and Valuation Department, bringing a total of those arrested to 12, following an on-going probe into a housing scam.
- The donor community says the political crisis in the country marks a very dangerous point in its history after a successful transition to multiparty politics.

- Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Cassim Chilumpha said in parliament on Thursday that cabinet ministers would challenge the Chief Justice if he granted an injunction to opposition parties to restrain parliament from sitting.
